The test image shows a corn ear with tip rot — brown/discolored kernels at the tip with white-gray mold growth, healthy yellow kernels below. This is an ear rot disease. Top candidates: Fusarium, Gibberella (tip rot with pink mold), Diplodia (white mold), Aspergillus (olive-green mold).

Let me view one reference from each top candidate.
Good match with Gibberella — tip rot, brown discolored kernels, white-gray mold. Very similar to test image. Let me check Fusarium and Diplodia for comparison.
Fusarium shows scattered mold in the middle of ear — doesn't match the tip rot pattern in the test. Now checking Diplodia Ear Rot.
Diplodia shows general ear drying, not the tip rot pattern. Gibberella remains the top match. Final reference — checking Aspergillus to rule out.

**Analysis:**
- **Test image**: Corn ear with tip rot — brown/rotted kernels concentrated at the tip, white-gray mold growth, healthy bright yellow kernels below. Classic tip-down rot pattern.
- **Gibberella** (ref): Near-identical — tip rot with brown discolored kernels, white-gray mycelium, healthy yellow kernels below. Gibberella ear rot classically starts at the tip and progresses downward.
- **Fusarium**: Scattered mid-ear white mold between kernels — doesn't match the tip-concentrated rot.
- **Diplodia**: General ear drying/straw coloration, not the discrete tip rot with mold mass shown here.
- **Aspergillus**: Distinctive olive-green powdery mold — clearly different from the test image's brownish rot with white-gray mold.
